title: Companion QA
eyebrow: Ready for your test · all nine steps of the companion build, version 0.4.0

unverified: Your real signed-in accounts have not been used. Every drive here used fake account folders and a stand-in script in place of Claude Code, because a real session needs a Claude login.
The orange Continue button has not carried a real session from one of your accounts to another.
The Android app has been built by GitHub but has never run on a phone, so the camera, notifications, battery use and the pause in the background are untested.
The phone link has only talked to the stand-in Claude Code, not the real one.
The Help pictures were taken from the fake-account drives, so the names in them are examples, not yours.

short.lead: All nine steps of the companion are built on top of version 0.3.0, and version 0.4.0 is ready to install. Each session can be shown as Claude Code's own terminal or as a calm Visual view with tap-to-answer cards. Every account works without switching, a full account hands its work to another with one tap, and a phone can pair with the PC. A Help page with a picture for each task replaces the first-run walkthrough.
short.hint: Tap an item to see what was checked and what it needs from you.
items: 196 pass, 0 fail and 3 are skipped here because they need Windows PowerShell. GitHub's Windows machine ran all of them, including those 3, and passed.
GitHub's Windows machine passed and built the installer

Until today the Windows run had never passed on the companion code. One phone link test built its folder path wrongly on Windows and then left a server open, which hung the whole run. The test is fixed, and a test that runs longer than 60 seconds now fails by name instead of hanging.
Each step driven here in the real app

Each step was driven here in the real app with fake accounts. The calm layer: 19 of 19 checks seen. Accounts: a session opened on its own account, a new one started on the chosen account, and a full account handed off. Phone link: 13 of 13 checks, with a phone-sized browser standing in for the phone. Help: opened twice in the app, with 11 cards, no broken pictures, and Escape closing it.

items: The installer replaces the version you have now. Your sessions stay where they are, because the app only reads your Claude folders.

Open https://github.com/Ajw2003/EdensProjectRouter/actions/runs/44446196918, scroll to Artifacts, download project-router-installer and unzip it. Run Project Router Setup 0.4.0.exe. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", click More info, then Run anyway.
Install the Android app on your phone
The APK is built by GitHub. It is not from the Play Store, so Android asks you to allow installs from your browser or file app once.
Open https://github.com/Ajw2003/EdensProjectRouter/actions/runs/44446181316 on the phone, download the APK artifact, unzip it and open EdensRouter.apk. Then follow Phone link below.
Every test below has a number and a picture. Tell me the number of anything that did not match.
Tap Copy my reply if all of it worked, or tell me the numbers that failed and what you saw.

changes: new
Test 2: Calm shell
A session list on the left and up to four sessions side by side.

Open the app. Tap a session to open it. Ctrl-click a second one, or tap Open beside, and check that the two sit side by side. Close one with its ×. Then quit and reopen the app, and check that the same sessions come back.
0.3.0 showed sessions as tiles in a grid.
A list and up to four panes.
Fewer things on screen, and the sessions you were in come back.

changes.alt: Two sessions open side by side next to the session list
changes.caption: Picture 2: two sessions side by side.

changes: new
Test 3: Visual view
The same session as messages and cards, with taps typed into Claude Code.

In a session with real Claude Code, tap Visual at its top left. Ask Claude something that makes it ask you a question. Check that a card with one button per answer appears, and that tapping one answers it in the Terminal too. Try Allow on a permission card, and Stop.
Only the terminal.
A Visual view beside the terminal, on the same live session.
Questions and permissions become buttons.

changes.alt: A question card in the Visual view with three answer buttons
changes.caption: Picture 3: a question card.

changes: new
Test 4: Visuals in the chat
Pictures and pages Claude makes appear in the conversation.

Ask Claude to make a small web page or picture in a project. Check that it shows in the Visual view, that a page opens in the side panel, and that the Files panel and the Pages shelf (both in the pane menu) list it.
Visuals lived in a separate tile.
They show in the chat where they were made.
You see Claude's work where you're already looking.

changes.alt: A picture and a page card inside the conversation
changes.caption: Picture 4: a picture and a page in the chat.

changes: new
Test 5: Needs you, focus card and What to show
The parts made for ADHD and autistic brains.

Leave a session waiting on a question. Check that it moves to Needs you at the top of the list and that a notification appears. Open More, then What to show…, try Calm, Balanced and Everything, and check that switches hide and show things without losing them.
Everything showed at once.
A Needs-you list, a focus card and switches for each kind of information.
Less to filter out, and nothing waiting goes unnoticed.

changes.alt: The Needs you group at the top of the session list
changes.caption: Picture 5: Needs you.

changes: new
Test 6: Accounts and Continue
New sessions pick an account with room; a full account hands its work on.

Tap New session. Check that the project list and the Suggested account look right for your accounts. When one account reaches its limit, check that an orange Continue on button appears, and that tapping it carries the work over with its earlier messages. Try Add account… with an account you already have, and check that it is refused.
You chose the account by hand and switched when one ran out.
A Suggested account, and a one-tap Continue when one is full.
Running out of usage no longer stops the work.

changes.alt: The orange Continue on button at the top of a session
changes.caption: Picture 6: Continue on another account.

changes: new
Test 7: Phone link
Your phone sees and answers the PC's sessions, with no Remote Control.

On the PC, open More, then Phone link: off (turn on), then Pair a phone…. Scan the code with the Android app. Check that the phone shows your sessions, that answering a question on the phone answers it on the PC, and that Unpair in the same box cuts the phone off.
There was no phone view.
A paired phone with the same Terminal and Visual views.
You can answer Claude from the sofa.

changes.alt: The Pair a phone box with a QR code
changes.caption: Picture 7: pairing a phone.

changes: new
Test 8: Android app
The phone screens as an installable app that notifies you.

After pairing, lock the phone and leave a session waiting on a question. Check that a notification arrives. Check the battery use after an hour, and what happens when the app has been in the background for a while.
Nothing on the phone.
An APK with Needs-you notifications.
You hear about questions without watching the screen.

changes.alt: The Android app's first screen asking to scan a pairing code
changes.caption: Picture 8: the Android app's first screen.

changes: new
Test 9: Help page
One card per task, each with a picture, in place of the walkthrough.
Check that no walkthrough opens on first launch. Tap Help at the bottom of the list, and check that the cards match what you see in the app. Press Escape, or tap Close, to shut it.
A three-step walkthrough that opened by itself.
A Help page that opens only when you ask.
Nothing interrupts you, and the answer is one tap away.
